hallucinations.claim: "Ollama 0.19 runs a 35B MoE model at slower speeds than MLX ... MLX providing roughly twice the decode speed of Ollama"
hallucinations.why: Ollama 0.19 (Mar 2026) switched its Mac backend to MLX on 32 GB+ Macs, roughly doubling its own speed and closing most of the gap; the 2x gap describes the old llama.cpp path.

hallucinations.claim: "you can comfortably load a full-precision Qwen 3.5-35B-A3B model"
hallucinations.why: A 35B model at BF16 is ~70 GB and does not fit in 48 GB; realistic is 4-bit (~17-20 GB).

hallucinations.claim: "If you quantise to Q4, the same machine can also handle a 70 B model at usable speeds"
hallucinations.why: Trap: a 70B Q4 is ~40 GB, leaves no headroom, swaps, and at 273 GB/s would decode only ~5-6 tok/s.

hallucinations.claim: "leaves about 44.5 GB for a model after macOS overhead"
hallucinations.why: Overstated; macOS's default GPU wired limit is about 75% of RAM (~36 GB) and the reference advises leaving 8-10 GB for the OS and apps.

great_answer_would: Say MLX is faster but Ollama 0.19+ now uses MLX on 32 GB+ Macs so check your version, give the 273 GB/s bandwidth rule (~15 tok/s for a 17 GB dense model, 60-100 for 3B-active MoE), cap at ~30-35B 4-bit, and flag slow long-prompt processing.
notes: Verdict 'MLX is faster' is technically defensible but the stated reason and both capacity claims are wrong; no flag about the 2026 Ollama change, which the asker specifically wants.

hallucinations.claim: "A 2017 systematic review of 18 studies found consistent evidence that magnesium supplementation lowered anxiety scores"
hallucinations.why: Boyle et al. 2017 covered 18 studies but only 8 on anxiety, 4 positive, all low quality; it called the evidence suggestive, not consistent.

hallucinations.claim: "200–400 mg elemental magnesium per day has been shown to reduce anxiety"
hallucinations.why: Overclaims: trials are small and mixed with no large RCT in diagnosed anxiety disorders.

hallucinations.claim: "most randomized trials using about 300 mg/day split into morning and evening doses"
hallucinations.why: Unverifiable; trial doses and regimens vary widely (the answer itself later says 75-360 mg).

hallucinations.claim: "taurate is highlighted for people who also have cardiovascular concerns" / "taurate may benefit those with cardiac issues"
hallucinations.why: Comes from supplement-marketing pages; no clinical evidence ties taurate to anxiety-plus-cardiac benefit.

what_went_wrong: Search leaned on supplement and rehab marketing pages alongside the Cureus review; the draft overstated the Boyle review and the merge laid it out as eight one-line paragraphs with no safety cautions.
great_answer_would: Lead with 200-350 mg elemental (glycinate or citrate, evening, 4-6 weeks), call the evidence weak (Boyle 2017: 4 of 8 low-quality studies positive), and flag the elemental-vs-compound label, the 350 mg supplemental UL and kidney disease.
notes: Dose range and 'no form proven superior' are right. Omitted citrate, oxide's poor absorption, the NIH 350 mg UL, elemental label caution and kidney warning. Final hedge partly redeems the overclaimed opening.
